name: Papas Guisadas (Mexican Stewed Potatoes)

ingredients.name: guajillo chiles
ingredients.prep: stemmed and seeded, and torn into pieces

instructions.primary_message: Cut the skinless boneless pork belly into 2-inch chunks. Peel and halve the white onion. Peel and cut the russet potatoes into 1-inch chunks. Stem, seed, and tear the guajillo chiles into pieces.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 lb skinless boneless pork belly
1 white onion
6 medium russet potatoes
2 guajillo chiles

instructions.primary_message: In a large stock pot or Dutch oven, combine pork belly, onion, garlic, stock, and 2 teaspoons salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat, reduce heat to maintain a simmer, and cook, covered, until pork belly can be easily pierced by a fork, about 1 1/2 hours. Add the potatoes and continue to simmer, stirring occasionally, until fork-tender, about 20 minutes.

Using a spider skimmer or slotted spoon, transfer pork and potatoes to a large bowl. Discard onion and garlic. Skim fat from the broth using a ladle or spoon (or pour through a fat separator and let it sit for 3 minutes to allow fat to float to the top). Reserve 3/4 cup of the broth, and reserve the remaining broth or for another use. Whip pot clean and set aside. Place pork on a cutting board and finely chop; return to bowl.

For the Sauce: In a blender jar, combine tomatoes, garlic, guajillos, cumin, oregano, and black peppercorns. Add the reserved 3/4 cup cooking liquid to the blender. Submerge the dried chiles in the liquid and let sit until chiles are slightly softened, about 5 minutes. Blend, starting at the lowest speed and gradually increasing to high, until smooth, about 1 minute. Season with salt to taste.

Pour sauce into the now-empty pot, then stir in pork and potatoes. Cook over medium-low heat until warmed through. Stir the stew to help combine ingredients: The more aggressively you stir, the creamier the dish will be (the final consistency is a matter of personal preference), but the sauce should at least be thick enough to coat the potatoes and pork. Adjust consistency with extra water or broth, if desired. Season to taste with salt. Serve, topping with cilantro and green onion.

description: This papas guisadas recipe pairs tender pork belly and potatoes with a smooth, guajillo-spiked tomato sauce for a rich, comforting Mexican stew.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Cilantro leaves, for garnish; Thinly sliced scallions, for garnish

Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → store-bought low-sodium chicken broth
author: Octavio Peña
